intro: You have arrived at the Ancient City of Klazomenai, an Ionian city at Urla in İzmir province. Its story runs in two layers: settlement at Liman Tepe goes back to the 4th millennium BC, while the city itself dates from the 8th century BC. This is the birthplace of the philosopher Anaxagoras, and a centre of early industrial olive oil production. Let us begin.
history: Settlement at Liman Tepe reaches back to the 4th millennium BC. Then, in the 5th century BC, fear changed everything: dreading the Persians, the inhabitants abandoned the mainland city and moved across to Karantina Island. Yet Klazomenai was never only a place of retreat. It struck some of the earliest silver coins in the 6th century BC and ran advanced olive oil workshops. Later, Alexander the Great bound the island to the mainland with a causeway.
structure-1: You are now at the Olive Oil Workshop. Here, olives were pressed into oil. Pause for a moment and imagine the steady work of pressing, and the oil that flowed from this place.
structure-4: Before you is the Liman Tepe Mound, a Bronze Age harbour settlement mound near Klazomenai. Beneath its layers lies the deepest chapter of this coast's story.
structure-5: Now look towards the Karantina Island Acropolis. This is the island acropolis that guarded the harbour of Klazomenai, keeping watch over the ships that came and went.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Theatre, and be sure to seek out the Temple too.
facts: Did you know? The olive oil workshop here dates to the 6th century BC, and with its 15 rock-cut pits it is among the earliest evidence of industrial-scale olive oil production, one of the oldest known anywhere. It has even been rebuilt and run experimentally, so the ancient process can be tried again. Anaxagoras came from here too: the philosopher who was put on trial in Athens for saying the sun was a red-hot stone. And finally, the painted terracotta 'Clazomenian sarcophagi' are rare witnesses to archaic painting.
outro: This brings our journey through the Ancient City of Klazomenai to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for listening, and enjoy the rest of your visit.
